speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; your history of cocaine, ecstasy use, and high-risk sexual behavior is concerning given your age and the acute agitation. Have you noticed any dark urine, pale stools, or specific neurological symptoms like confusion or tremors in addition to the jaundice? Also, when exactly did you last consume alcohol or recreational drugs?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis (likely Viral Hepatitis B given high-risk sexual behavior and jaundice, with agitation potentially secondary to encephalopathy or drug withdrawal).
